title: Tight Upper Bounds on Color Reversal by Local Inversions
summary: A bicoloration of a graph $G=(V,E)$ is a map $β:V\to\{-1,1\}$. A local inversion at a vertex $v$ complements the subgraph induced by the neighbors of $v$ and simultaneously reverses the colors of all neighbors of $v$. Sabidussi (Discrete Mathematics, 1987) showed that every bicolored graph on $n$ vertices without isolated vertices admits a color reversal using at most $6n+3$ local inversions, and that any two bicolorings of such a graph can be transformed into each other using at most $9n$ local inversions. Recently, Porte, Sandeep, and Santra (CALDAM 2026) improved these bounds to $4n-3$…
